y1: After John was arrested, Jesus moved to Capernaum and began His ministry. Matthew quotes Isaiah 9:1–2: “The people who sat in darkness saw a great light.”
y2: Galilee was a remote area where various nations lived, so much so that it was called “Galilee of the Gentiles.” The light fell first on the outskirts, not on the elite of Jerusalem.
y3: The land of Zebulun and Naphtali was the first place trampled by Assyria in the 8th century BC. The light came first to the place that fell into darkness first. God begins restoration where the wound is deepest.
y5: At that time, to become a disciple of a rabbi, a student would go to the teacher and ask to be accepted. But Jesus approached the working fishermen Himself and said, “Follow Me.”
y6: Peter and Andrew “immediately” left their nets and followed Him. Matthew emphasizes this word “immediately” twice.
y7: Jesus turned what they were good at, catching fish, into a new mission. The call sometimes requires us to leave what we have, and sometimes it calls us to use it in a new way for the kingdom of God.
y9: James and John were mending their nets with their father Zebedee. This was a family business large enough to have hired men {Mark 1:20}.
y10: They left the boat and their father and followed Him. There was a cost to following: job, security, and family expectations.
y11: This scene is not a command to abandon one's family. It is a confession that Jesus is above everything. Later, Zebedee's wife also became one of those who followed Jesus (27:56).
y13: Jesus traveled all over Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of heaven, and healing every kind of disease.
y14: The news spread to Syria, the Decapolis, and across the Jordan. Jews and Gentiles came together.
y15: 4:23 and 9:35 are almost the exact same sentence. Between them come Jesus' “teaching” (chapters 5–7, the Sermon on the Mount) and “healings” (chapters 8–9, miracles). By showing word and deed together, Matthew proves who Jesus is.
verse: “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.” They immediately left their nets and followed Him.
prayer: Jesus, thank You for first seeking and calling people whom no one else would choose. Help me to leave the nets that hold me back and follow You. Let me use the things I am good at to lead people to salvation. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ, who called me. Amen.
d0: Capernaum. It was a village on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, and Peter's house was there. It is called Jesus' “own city” (9:1). Today, the remains of a first-century synagogue and Peter's house have been found there.
d1: Galilee. It was a region despised by the people of Jerusalem because various nations lived there. The Galilean accent was also mocked (26:73). Most of Jesus' twelve disciples were from Galilee.
d2: rabbi. A teacher who gathered disciples and taught the Law. The disciple lived with the teacher and learned his words and life. The disciples called Jesus “Rabbi.”
d3: disciple. Not just a student who learns knowledge, but a person who walks with the teacher and tries to become like him in life. The Gospel of Matthew ends with the words “make disciples of all nations” (28:19).
d4: synagogue. The temple was only in Jerusalem, but there was a synagogue in every village. They gathered there on the Sabbath to read the Word. Jesus often taught in synagogues.
d5: Gospel. It was originally a word announcing victory in war or the accession of a new king. Jesus announced that God had come as King. In Azerbaijani, it is called “Müjdə”.
